newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-INDIAN FIGHT BACK LED BY AZHARUDDIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIAN FIGHT BACK LED BY AZHARUDDIN.

text.p: A stirring eighth-wicket stand of 141 runs between Mohammad Azharuddin and Anil Kumble led India's fight back against South Africa on the third day of the second test at Calcutta on Friday.
India put on 150 runs in just two hours to lunch with a display of scintillating strokes, scuttling the visitors' hopes of enforcing the follow-on.
The home side's first innings ended at 329 shortly after lunch having gone into the interval at 302 for seven.
They began the day at 152 for six, requiring 77 runs to make South Africa bat again. Overnight batsman Javagal Srinath did not last long and was bowled by Allan Donald for 11.

Azharuddin, who retired hurt on Thursday after being hit on the arm by Brian McMillan, then walked in to play one of the finest innings seen at Eden Gardens, scoring a well-deserved century, his 15th, in the process.
Peppered by short-pitched deliveries by the South Africans seeking to expose his weakness against the short rising ball, Azharuddin unleashed a series of pulls to demoralise the opposition.

All bowlers came in for punishment with Lance Klusener singled out for special treatment. The South African debutant was hit for 21 runs in one over as Azharuddin displayed the full range of his wristy strokes.
His partner Anil Kumble was not far behind as he displayed skills befitting a top-order batsman, handling pace and spin with equal ease. Kumble was out at 88.
It was a disappointing session for the South Africans, who started the day aiming to polish off the Indian innings.
Instead they were put to the sword by one of the finest displays of attacking batsmanship seen on Indian grounds.
